baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated mawla at words 4 and 10 is predicated positively of Allah for believers and then negated for disbelievers.
baseline_models.mechanism: The W-L-Y branches of gapless proximity and taking charge combine with the settled trust of A-M-N. The positive half therefore names an immediately present custodian who assumes the believers' affair, while truth-covering leaves the other group without a corresponding custodian.

activation_trace.role: Gapless proximity makes the repeated mawla an immediate relation rather than remote sponsorship.
Taking charge of an affair supplies the custodial function carried by that nearness.
Settled security and trust describe the human posture capable of inhabiting the custodial relation.
Covering or blocking truth supplies the relational obstruction on the negated side.

changed_reading.before: Allah is generically the believers' protector, whereas disbelievers have none.
changed_reading.after: Allah is the believers' immediately near custodian who assumes their affair; the contrasting group has no such operative relation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Mawla is the shared pivot of the verse's balanced positive and negative clauses.
baseline_models.mechanism: The alliance branch of W-L-Y makes mawla a bond of love, loyalty, and effective aid rather than a bare title. A-M-N supplies trusted assent, while K-F-R can supply disavowal; the verse contrasts an enacted allegiance with relational repudiation.

activation_trace.role: Love, support, and allegiance make mawla an active solidaristic bond.
Heart-settling assent provides the believers' side of allegiance.
Disavowal and dissociation make the negative side a ruptured bond, not merely a different opinion.

changed_reading.before: The verse assigns two groups different labels and different protection.
changed_reading.after: The verse contrasts effective allegiance to Allah with a disavowal that leaves no functioning alliance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The noun mawla occurs in a construction of possession or benefit: Allah is mawla of one group, while no mawla is theirs.
baseline_models.mechanism: W-L-Y also carries recognized kinship, clientage, emancipation ties, and priority or entitlement. On that branch, the contrast concerns standing: believers possess a valid patronal bond and a party with first claim upon them, whereas the negated group has no effective or rightful sponsor.

activation_trace.role: Kinship, clientage, emancipation, and neighborhood supply a recognized social or juridical bond.
Priority and entitlement supply the question of whose claim is rightful and effective.
The worshipped deity is explicitly identified as the holder of the positive patronal relation.

changed_reading.before: Mawla means only a rescuer in danger.
changed_reading.after: Mawla can also mark recognized patronage, standing, and a rightful first claim, all of which are denied on the second side.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context prevents K-F-R from remaining a one-note image. The focus group's covering blocks truth, but the same root at 47:2 depicts faults being covered away for believers; later a screened garden and fault-covering forgiveness extend protective concealment. The mawla relation can therefore be read as changing the function of covering from obstruction into shelter and release from fault.

activation_trace.role: Truth-blocking supplies the harmful covering named on the focus verse's negative side.
Custodial agency supplies the one who can redirect covering toward preservation.
Covering misdeeds until their effect is removed reverses the focus root's obstructive function.
A garden screened by growth turns concealment into inhabitable shelter.
Protective covering of fault confirms the beneficial counterpart to truth-covering.

structural_cues: 47:2 places believers and divine covering of their faults in one coordinated description, while 47:6 and 47:15 continue the shelter-and-forgiveness sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposing K-F-R branches and later protective coverings; I supply the arrow that patronage transforms the function of covering. A live alternative is simple root polysemy with no causal link to mawla.

changed_reading.before: Disbelievers cover truth and therefore simply lack a protector.
changed_reading.after: The contrast also turns on who can convert covering into mercy: the mawla covers faults and provides shelter, while self-directed truth-covering has no redemptive cover behind it.

context_deltas.mechanism: Guidance, repair, admission, and settled residence occur as an ordered chain around the focus. Read through W-L-Y's administration and continuity branches, mawla governs a whole trajectory rather than appearing only at a moment of danger.

activation_trace.role: Taking charge of an affair makes the ordered outcomes functions of custodianship.
Uninterrupted succession supplies continuity across the stages.
Gentle direction toward a path supplies the route's first stage.
Repair against corruption supplies internal restoration during the route.
Passage into an interior supplies successful admission rather than mere approach.
Residence and stable emplacement supply the terminal condition of the trajectory.

structural_cues: The short consecutive clauses of 47:5-6 move from guidance through repair to entry, and 47:12 contrasts the two groups by destination and residence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an ordered series of acts and destinations; I assign their sequence as the operational scope of mawla. They could alternatively be separate promised outcomes rather than one custodial process.

changed_reading.before: The mawla intervenes episodically to protect believers.
changed_reading.after: The mawla continuously administers a passage from orientation and repair through admission to lasting placement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context places reciprocal aid inside a test and gives it a bodily result: believers aid Allah's cause, receive aid, and have their feet fixed. The alliance reading of mawla becomes participatory and stabilizing, not passive insulation from trial.

activation_trace.role: Support and allegiance supply the reciprocal social mechanism.
A test that makes condition visible supplies the setting in which allegiance becomes observable.
Aid appears on both sides of the conditional sequence and operationalizes the alliance.
Strengthening and fixing supply the effect of received support.
The physical foot localizes stabilization in continued action and stance.

structural_cues: 47:7 uses a conditional protasis and apodosis with the same aid root, followed immediately by fixed feet.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal aid, testing, and stabilization; I read these as enactments of the focus alliance. An alternative is that aid is a discrete command-and-reward relation rather than the content of mawla.

changed_reading.before: Believers are protected without their own allegiance becoming part of the mechanism.
changed_reading.after: Mawla names an alliance enacted under test: committed aid is answered by support that steadies further action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The negative half of the focus becomes a failure of recovery rather than an abstract lack of company. The sequence moves through a fall without rising, collapse of works, complete destruction, and a settlement whose gathered strength yields no helper. No mawla means no effective backstop when a trajectory fails.

activation_trace.role: Effective aid supplies the missing backstop in the negated clause.
Truth-blocking anchors the affected group in the focus rather than making collapse an independent theme.
Stumbling without recovery gives concrete motion to the absence of a backstop.
Descent and collapse transfer the failure from bodies to the efficacy of works.
Comprehensive ruin supplies the endpoint when no recovery intervenes.
Strength gathered like strands of rope supplies the failed substitute for patronage.
The explicit absence of an aider resolves no mawla into failed rescue despite worldly force.

structural_cues: 47:8-10 place fall, failed works, and ruin immediately before the focus, and 47:13 repeats the no-X-for-them construction after naming superior strength.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies escalating failures and an explicit absent helper; I connect them as the practical meaning of no mawla. They may instead be parallel consequences without a single backstop mechanism.

changed_reading.before: No mawla means only that disbelievers lack companionship or favorable affiliation.
changed_reading.after: No mawla means that neither works nor accumulated power has an effective recovery agent when collapse begins.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first depicts diversion from a traversable path and opposed acts of following; later the W-L-Y root itself appears as turning away, immediately followed by corruption and cutting kinship. The focus's no-mawla can therefore be carried as the endpoint of enacted distance and severed bonds, not only an externally imposed deprivation.

activation_trace.role: Gapless nearness supplies the relation that directional choices either sustain or undo.
Turning away and diverting initiate movement away from the focus relation.
A path extended for traversal supplies the spatial axis along which diversion operates.
Following directly behind supplies the opposed trajectories of the two groups.
The same root's turning-away branch exposes the reversible orientation latent in mawla.
Severing connection converts inward turning-away into social rupture.
Kinship identifies the concrete bond damaged by that rupture.

structural_cues: The two groups repeatedly occupy parallel follow-or-divert constructions, and 47:22 places turning away before corruption and kin-cutting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies path diversion, opposed following, and a W-L-Y turn followed by severance; I infer a trajectory from chosen distance to no patronal bond. A live alternative is that these are separate moral symptoms rather than a causal sequence.

changed_reading.before: The absence of a mawla is assigned to a fixed group from outside.
changed_reading.after: The absence can also be read dynamically: diversion and turning away produce distance, then become the cutting of the very bonds patronage would sustain.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later awla occurrence activates W-L-Y's priority and entitlement branch, and the next verse answers with obedience and truth enacted in deed. This strengthens the baseline possibility that Allah as mawla is not only one who helps but the one whose claim comes first and is realized by responsive action.

activation_trace.role: Priority and entitlement supply the latent claim dimension of mawla.
Recognized clientage and kin-like standing give that claim a relational form.
The contextual root occurrence directly reactivates what is more fitting, prior, or entitled.
Obedient yielding supplies the response by which a prior claim becomes operative.
Making truth good in action tests whether professed patronage is real.

structural_cues: The awla phrase closes 47:20 and is followed immediately by obedience, recognized speech, resolve, and truthful action in 47:21.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the W-L-Y priority branch and the immediate obedience sequence; I read obedience as answering Allah's prior claim. The awla phrase may instead be an independent evaluative formula with no backward lexical pressure on mawla.

changed_reading.before: Mawla answers only the question of who will help.
changed_reading.after: Mawla may also answer who has the first rightful claim, with obedience and truthful action disclosing whether that patronage is acknowledged.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing context breaks any model of patronage as mutual need. Opposition cannot diminish Allah; he does not diminish believers' works or need their wealth; he is self-sufficient while they are needy. If they turn away, another people can stand in their place. Mawla is thus a giving, nonextractive custodianship whose human participants remain replaceable.

activation_trace.role: Taking charge supplies the patronal function whose asymmetry the context exposes.
Loss or diminution is explicitly unavailable against Allah, removing divine vulnerability from the alliance.
Deprivation that strips a right or work is denied, making the patron preserve rather than extract value.
Accumulated wealth supplies the material stake that the surrounding negation denies as Allah's need.
Self-sufficiency establishes that the patronal side lacks no resource supplied by clients.
Need and scant means identify the human side as the beneficiary rather than Allah's necessary support.
Turning away makes continued participation in patronage conditional on orientation.
One thing standing in another's place supplies actual replaceability.
Deputizing or standing in another's place gives the replacement a social bearer.

structural_cues: 47:35 says Allah is with the believers while preserving their works; 47:36 negates a demand for their wealth; 47:38 opposes divine sufficiency to human need and places replacement in an if-then construction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-harm, non-deprivation, wealth negation, sufficiency, need, turning, and replacement; I infer these define the economy of mawla. They could alternatively be separate exhortations that qualify discipleship without defining patronage.

changed_reading.before: Divine alliance resembles reciprocal patronage in which both sides need the other's resources.
changed_reading.after: Allah's patronage gives and preserves without needing extraction; humans need the bond, yet any participants who turn away can be replaced.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets W-L-Y's specialized follow-on-rain branch color the nominal mawla; it remains anchored in the focus root and is activated by the immediately following garden, flow, and river images. Downstream prose should mark it as an ecological analogy, not a lexical translation of mawla.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus mawla is carried through the W-L-Y branch for rain that follows the first seasonal rain.

activation_trace.role: Rain following earlier rain supplies an image of sustaining continuation latent in the focus root.
A tree-screened garden supplies the land made inhabitable by continued water.
Continuing provision and gift turn water flow into sustained care rather than one event.
A river cutting the land with running water supplies the ecological result.
The fourfold river occurrence amplifies regenerative continuity into an environment.

changed_reading.before: Mawla is an abstract personal protector.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, mawla is like the sustaining rain that follows an initiating rain: patronage continues trust into a flowing, habitable ecology, while the negative side lacks that regenerative sequel.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the W-L-Y saddle-underlay branch through the context's war burden; it remains anchored in the focus mawla and yields a coherent support mechanism. Downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for hidden load-bearing support, never as the noun's direct gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus mawla is tested against W-L-Y's image of the layer placed beneath a saddle on an animal's back.

activation_trace.role: The under-saddle layer supplies hidden support immediately beneath a carried load.
War's burdens supply the load that presses until it is laid down.
Weight that weakens supplies the pressure against which under-support matters.

changed_reading.before: Protection is imagined only as an external shield or rescuer.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, mawla can be imaged as support directly under the bearer of a heavy trial, enabling the burden to be carried until it is put down.

strongest_changes: The K-F-R contrast reverses internally: harmful truth-covering is answered by fault-covering, shelter, and forgiveness under divine custodianship.
Mawla expands from episodic rescue into an administered route of guidance, repair, entry, residence, reciprocal aid, and stabilized action.
No mawla becomes both the lack of a recovery backstop and the relational result of diversion, turning away, and severed bonds.
The closing sequence makes patronage radically asymmetric: Allah is unharmed and self-sufficient, preserves rather than extracts, and can replace participants who turn away.
summary.what_was_special: The most productive activations came from root reversals and recurrences rather than topic matching: K-F-R changes the moral function of covering, and W-L-Y moves among nearness, alliance, priority, turning away, and replacement. The repeated mawla thus supports several live mechanisms without requiring them to collapse into one gloss.
remaining_uncertainties: The ordered contextual outcomes may describe consequences of patronage without each being part of mawla's lexical content.
The priority reading from awla is plausible but remains more form-sensitive than the proximity, administration, and support readings.
The rain and saddle-underlay models are branch-distant analogies and require explicit exploratory qualification.
The negation may deny every patron absolutely or, more narrowly, every effective and rightful patron; the packet keeps both scopes live.
